zh: 七姑奶奶亦正有此意。找个空隙，打断他们的谈锋，说了两句做女主人应有的门面话，与罗四姐双双席席。七姑奶奶将她带到楼上卧室。这间卧室一直为罗四姐所欣赏，因为经过古应春设计，改成西式，有个很宽敞的阳台，装置很大的玻璃门，门上加两层帷幕、一层薄纱、一层丝绒，白天拉开丝绒那一层，阳光透过薄纱，铺满整个房间，明亮华丽，令人精神一爽。晚上坐在阳台上看万家灯火，亦别有一番情趣，尤其是象这种夏天，在阳台上纳凉闲谈，是最舒服不过的一件事。“你是喝中国茶，还是喝洋茶？”所谓“喝洋茶”是英国式的奶茶。七姑奶奶有全套的银茶具，照英国规矩亲自调制，而且亲自为客人倒茶，颇为费事。罗四姐此刻要谈正事，无心欣赏“洋茶”，便即说道：“我想吃杯菊花茶。”黄白“杭菊花”可以当茶叶泡来喝，有清心降火之功，七姑奶奶笑着问道：“你大概心里很乱？”“也不晓得啥道理，心里一直烦躁。”“我们到阳台上来坐。”七姑奶奶挑到阳台上去密谈，是替罗四姐设想，因为谈到自己的终身大事，她难免腼腆，阳台上光线幽暗，可以隐藏妞促的表情，就比较能畅所欲言了。
en: The Seventh Lady had been thinking the same thing. Finding a pause, she interrupted the men's flow of talk with a few of the gracious remarks expected of a hostess, and the two women left the table. She took Luo Sijie upstairs to her bedroom, which Luo had always admired. Gu Yingchun had redesigned it in the Western style, with a spacious balcony and large glass doors hung with two layers of curtains, one gauze and the other velvet. When the velvet curtains were drawn back by day, sunlight passed through the gauze and filled the room, making it bright, splendid, and wonderfully refreshing. At night, the sight of countless lights from the balcony had a charm of its own. In summer, especially, nothing could be more comfortable than sitting there in the cool air and talking. “Will you have Chinese tea or foreign tea?” Foreign tea meant English tea with milk. The Seventh Lady had a complete silver tea service and followed the English custom of preparing the tea herself and pouring it for her guests, a rather elaborate business. Luo, intent on discussing serious matters, had no mind to appreciate it. “I'd like a cup of chrysanthemum tea.” The yellow and white Hangzhou chrysanthemums could be brewed like tea to calm the mind and dispel internal heat. “Is your mind rather unsettled?” the Seventh Lady asked with a smile. “I don't know why, but I've been feeling restless all this time.” “Let's sit out on the balcony.” She chose the balcony out of consideration for Luo. Discussing her own marriage was bound to make her shy; in the dim light she could conceal her embarrassment and speak more freely.

zh: 等小大姐泡了菊花茶来，背光坐着的罗四姐幽幽地叹口气说：“七姐只怕我真的是命中注定了。”“喔，”七姑奶奶问道：“胡家托乌先生来作媒了，他怎么说？”“他说的话也不晓得是真是假？说胡大先生的意思，要我去替他当家。”“不错，这话应春也听见的。”“这么说，看起来是真的！”罗四姐心里更加踏实，但心头的疑虑亦更浓重，“七姐，你说。 我凭啥资格去替他当家？”七姑奶奶心想，胡雪岩顾虑者在此，罗四姐要争者亦在此，足见都是厉害角色，不开口则已，一开口必中要害。不过，她虽然已从古应春口中摸透了“行情”，却不愿轻易松口，因为不知道罗四姐还会开什么条件，不能不谨慎行事。于是她试探地问道：“四姐，你自己倒说呢？要啥资格，才好去替他当家。”“当家人的身分，身分不高，下人看不起，你说的话他左耳进、右耳出，七姐，你说，这个家我怎么当？”“是的。这话很实在。我想，我们小爷叔，不会不懂这个道理，他总有让下人敬重你的办法。”
en: When the maid had brought their chrysanthemum tea, Luo, sitting with her face turned away from the light, gave a soft sigh. “Seventh Sister, perhaps it really is my destiny.” “Oh? The Hu family has asked Mr Wu to act as matchmaker. What did he say?” “I don't know whether to believe him. He said Mr Hu wanted me to run his household.” “That's true. Yingchun heard him say it too.” “Then it seems he really means it!” Luo felt more assured, yet her misgivings grew stronger. “Tell me, Seventh Sister, what standing would I have to run his household?” This, the Seventh Lady reflected, was precisely what troubled Hu Xueyan and what Luo meant to fight for. They were both formidable people: once either of them spoke, the words went straight to the heart of the matter. Although Gu had already told her exactly how things stood, she was unwilling to commit herself too readily. She did not know what further conditions Luo might put forward, so caution was necessary. “What do you think yourself?” she asked tentatively. “What standing would you need to manage the household?” “It is the housekeeper's position that matters. If your rank is low, the servants look down on you. Everything you say goes in one ear and out the other. Tell me, how could I run a household like that?” “Yes, that's a very practical consideration. I don't suppose Little Uncle fails to understand it. He will find some way to make the servants respect you.”

zh: “啥办法？”罗四姐紧接着问，“七姐夫怎么说？”“他说，胡老太太托我来做媒。不过，我还不敢答应。”罗四姐又惊又喜，“原来是胡老太太出面？”她问：“胡太太呢？”“他们家一切都是老太太作主。胡太太最贤惠不过，老太太说啥就是啥，百依百顺的。”听得这一说，罗四姐心头宽松了些，不过七姑奶奶何以不敢答应做媒？这话她却不好意思问。“我为啥不敢答应呢？”七姑奶奶自问自答他说：“因为我们虽然一见如故，象同胞姐妹一样，到底这是你的终身大事，你没有跟我详详细细谈过，我不晓得你心里的想法，如果冒冒失失答应下来，万一做不成这个媒，反而伤了我们感情。”“七姐，这一层你尽管放心。不管怎么样，你我的感情是不会伤的。”“有你这句话，我的胆就大了。四姐，除了名分以外，还有啥？请你一样一样告诉我。看哪一样是我可以代为答应下来的，哪一样我能替你争的，哪一样是怎么样也办不到的。”
en: “What way?” Luo asked at once. “What did Brother-in-Law Gu say?” “He said Old Madam Hu had asked me to act as matchmaker. But I haven't dared agree yet.” Luo was both startled and delighted. “So Old Madam Hu herself is behind this? What about Mrs Hu?” “The old lady decides everything in their household. Mrs Hu is as virtuous as can be. Whatever the old lady says, she accepts; she obeys her in everything.” Luo felt easier on hearing this. But why had the Seventh Lady not dared accept the commission? She was too embarrassed to ask. “Why haven't I dared agree?” the Seventh Lady went on, answering her own question. “Though we felt like old friends from the moment we met, as close as real sisters, this is still your marriage, a matter for your whole life. You haven't talked it over with me in detail, so I don't know exactly what you want. If I rashly agreed and then failed to arrange the match, it might end by hurting our friendship.” “Seventh Sister, you can put that fear aside. Whatever happens, it will never hurt the friendship between us.” “That gives me courage. Sister Luo, apart from your formal status, what else is there? Tell me everything, one thing at a time. Then we can see what I can agree to on their behalf, what I can try to obtain for you, and what cannot possibly be done.”

zh: “怎么佯办不到的事，我也不会说。”罗四姐想了一下说：“七姐，我顶为难的是我老娘。”她老娘何以会成为难题？七姑奶奶想一想才明白，必是指的当亲戚来往这件事。以她的看法，这件事是否为难，主要的是要看罗四姐自己的态度？倘或她坚持要胡老太太叫一声“亲家太太”，这就为难了！否则胡家也容易处置。谈到这里，话就要明说了，“四姐，你的意思我懂了。”她说：“还有啥，你一股脑儿说出来，我们一样一样来商量。”“还有，你晓得的，我有个女儿。”“你的女儿当然姓她老子的姓。”七姑奶奶说：“你总不见得肯带到胡家去吧？”“当然，那算啥一出？”“既然不带到胡家，那就是你自己的事，不管你怎么安排，胡家都不便过问的。这件事可以不必谈，还有啥？”
en: “I wouldn't ask for anything impossible.” Luo thought for a moment. “My mother is my greatest difficulty.” Why should her mother present a difficulty? After a little thought, the Seventh Lady understood: Luo must mean whether the two families would acknowledge each other as relatives by marriage. In her view, whether this became a problem depended chiefly on Luo's own attitude. If she insisted that Old Madam Hu address her mother as a fellow mother-in-law, that would indeed be difficult. Otherwise, the Hu family could easily manage it. At this point, they had to speak plainly. “I understand what you mean. What else is there? Tell me everything, and we'll discuss the points one by one.” “Then there's my daughter, as you know.” “Your daughter naturally bears her father's surname,” said the Seventh Lady. “Surely you wouldn't want to take her into the Hu household?” “Of course not. What sort of arrangement would that be?” “Since you won't be bringing her into their household, she is your own concern. Whatever arrangements you make, the Hu family would have no business interfering. We needn't discuss that. What else?”

zh: “还有，我只能给老太太一个人磕头。”“是不是！”七姑奶奶马上接口，“我不敢答应，就是怕你有这样的话，叫我说都不便去说的。”罗四姐自己也觉得要求过分了一些，不过话既已出口，亦不便自己收回，因而保持沉默。当然，在七姑奶奶看，这就是不再坚持的表示，能商量得通的。“四姐，我现在把人家的意思告诉你：第一是称呼，下人部叫你太太，第二进门磕一个头，以后都是平礼，第三生了儿子着红裙。这三洋，是老太大交代下来的。”罗四姐考虑了一会，觉得就此三事而言，再争也争不出什么名堂来，不如放漂亮些，换取对方在他处的让步。于是她说：“七姐这么说，我听七姐的。不过，我进他家的门，不晓得是怎么个进法？”
en: “One more thing: I can kowtow to the old lady, but to no one else.” “There!” the Seventh Lady replied immediately. “That is just why I was afraid to agree. I feared you might say something like this, a condition I couldn't even bring myself to put to them.” Luo herself felt she had asked a little too much. Having said it, however, she could hardly withdraw it of her own accord, so she remained silent. To the Seventh Lady, this naturally meant that she was no longer insisting and could be persuaded. “Now let me tell you what the family proposes. First, the form of address: all the servants will call you Madam. Second, you will make the required kowtow when you first enter the household; after that, all greetings will be exchanged as between equals. Third, once you have borne a son, you may wear a red skirt. These three instructions come from the old lady herself.” Luo considered them for a while. She felt that, on these three points, no amount of argument would gain her anything further. Better to concede gracefully and obtain concessions elsewhere. “If that is what you say, Seventh Sister, I'll accept your advice. But how exactly am I to enter their household?”

zh: 七姑奶奶心想，这是明知故问。妾侍进门，无非一乘一轿抬进门，在红烛高烧之下，一一磕头定称呼。罗四姐问到这话，意思是不是想要坐花轿进门呢？当然，照一般的办法，是太委屈了她，但亦决无坐花轿之理。七姑奶奶觉得这才真的遇见难题了。想了又想，七姑奶奶只能这佯回答：“这件事我来想办法，总归要让你面子上看得过去。你明天倒问问乌先生，看他有啥好办法？”正事谈到这里，实在也可以说是很顺利了。做媒本来就要往返磋商，一步一步将双方意见接近来，罗四姐也很明白事缓则圆的道理，因而很泰然地答说：“事情不急，七姐尽管慢慢想。”“你是不急，小爷叔恐怕急着要想做新郎官。”七姑奶奶笑着将她的脸扳向亮处，“不晓得你装扮成新娘子，是个啥样子？”这话说得罗四姐心里不知是何滋味？说一句：“七姐真会寻开心。”一闪站起身来，“乌先生不知道吃好了没有？”“我们一起下去看看。”
en: The Seventh Lady thought that Luo knew the answer perfectly well. A concubine was carried into the house in an ordinary sedan chair and, before the blazing red candles, made the kowtows that established her rank and the proper forms of address. Was Luo asking because she wanted to arrive in a decorated bridal chair? Certainly the ordinary procedure would be too humiliating for her, but there could be no question of the bridal chair either. Here, the Seventh Lady felt, was a real difficulty. After much thought, she could only say, “I'll try to find a way. Whatever we do, it must preserve your dignity. Ask Mr Wu tomorrow and see whether he has a good idea.” Their discussion had, in fact, gone very smoothly. Matchmaking always required negotiation back and forth, bringing the two sides closer step by step. Luo understood that patience gave matters time to come right. “There's no hurry,” she answered calmly. “Take your time thinking it over.” “You may not be in a hurry, but Little Uncle is probably eager to become a bridegroom.” With a smile, the Seventh Lady turned Luo's face toward the light. “I wonder what you'll look like dressed as a bride.” Luo could hardly have described the feelings this stirred in her. “You do love teasing me!” she said, springing to her feet. “I wonder whether Mr Wu has finished his dinner.” “Let's go down together and see.”

zh: 两人携着手夏回楼下，只见古应春陪着乌先生在赏鉴那些西洋小摆设。七姑奶奶少不得问些吃饭了没有之类的客气话，然后间到乌先生下榻之处。“客栈已经定好了。”古应春问道：“不知道罗四姐今天晚上，是不是还有事要跟乌先生谈？”“今天太晚了。”罗四姐答说：“有事明天也可以谈。”“那么，我送乌先生回客栈。明天一早我会派人到客栈陪了乌先主到罗四姐那里。下午我陪乌先生到各处逛逛。”等古应春送客回来，七姑奶奶还没有睡，等着要将与罗四姐谈论的情形告诉他，最后谈到罗四姐如何“进胡家的门”。“一顶小轿抬进门，东也磕头，西也磕头，且不说罗四姐委屈，我们做媒人的也没有面子。”“为小爷叔，没有面子也就算了。”古应春说：“你不要把你的想法也摆进去，那一来事情就越发摆不平了。”“好！那么罗四姐，总要让他的面子过得去。”“这有点难办。又有里子，又要面子，世界上恐怕没有那么便宜的事。”七姑奶奶也觉得丈夫的话不错，不过已经答应罗四姐要让她“面子上过得去。”所以仍在苦苦思索。“睡吧！我累了。”古应春旅途劳顿，一上床，鼾声即起，七姑奶奶却无法合眼，最后终于想到了一个办法，而且自己觉得很得意，很想唤醒古应春来谈，却又不忍，只好闷在心里。
en: Hand in hand, they went downstairs, where Gu Yingchun was showing Mr Wu his little Western ornaments. The Seventh Lady made the customary inquiries about whether their guest had eaten enough, then asked where he was staying. “His room at the inn has already been booked,” Gu said. “Does Sister Luo have anything else she wants to discuss with Mr Wu tonight?” “It's too late tonight. Anything we need to discuss can wait until tomorrow.” “Then I'll take Mr Wu back to his inn. First thing tomorrow, I'll send someone there to accompany him to your house. In the afternoon, I'll show him around.” When Gu returned from seeing their guest home, the Seventh Lady was still awake, waiting to tell him about her conversation with Luo. She ended with the question of how Luo was to enter the Hu household. “To be carried in in a little chair and made to kowtow here, there, and everywhere—quite apart from the humiliation to Sister Luo, it would do us matchmakers no credit.” “For Little Uncle's sake, we can put up with losing a little face,” Gu said. “Don't add your own feelings to the problem. That will only make it harder to settle.” “Very well! But at least Sister Luo must be allowed to keep her dignity.” “That's rather difficult. To get both the substance and all the outward honours—I'm afraid there are few bargains as good as that in this world.” The Seventh Lady knew her husband had a point, but she had promised Luo a dignified arrangement and went on searching for a solution. “Go to sleep. I'm tired,” Gu said. Exhausted by his journey, he began to snore as soon as he was in bed. She could not close her eyes. At last she hit upon an idea of which she was particularly proud. She wanted to wake him and discuss it, but could not bear to disturb him, so she kept it to herself.

zh: 第二天一早，古应春正在漱洗时，七姑奶奶醒了，掀开珠罗纱的帐子，探头说道：“不要紧了！我有法子了。”没头没脑一句话，说得古应春愣在那里，好一会才省悟，“你是说罗四姐？”他问。“对。”七姑奶奶起床，倦眼惺松，但脸上别有一种兴奋的神情，“他们的喜事在上海办，照两头大的办法，一样可以坐花轿、着红裙。”她问：“你看呢？”“小爷叔在杭州有大太大的，无人不知，人家问起来怎么说？”“兼桃！”七姑奶奶脱口回答：“哪个去查他们的家谱？”“这话倒也是。不知道小爷叔肯不肯？”“肯不肯是他自己的事，我们做媒人的，是有交代了。”七姑奶奶又说：“我想他也不会不肯的。”古应春考虑了一会，同意了她的办法，只问：“回到杭州呢？”“照回门的办法，先到祖宗堂磕头，再见老太太磕头。”“这不是哈回门的办法，是‘庙见’，这就抬举罗四姐的身分了。”古应春深深点头：“可以！”“你说可以就定规了。下半天，你问问乌先生，看他怎么说。”“能这样，乌先生还有什么话说？至到你说‘走规’，这话是错了，要小爷叔答应了才能定规。”“你这么说，那就快写信去问。”古应春觉得不必如此匆促。不过，这一点他觉得也不必跟爱妻去争，反正是不是写了信，她也不会知道，所以答应着说：“我会写。”
en: Early the next morning, while Gu was washing, the Seventh Lady awoke, drew aside the gauze bed curtains, and poked out her head. “It's all right now! I've found a way.” Gu stared, bewildered by this announcement without preamble. After a moment he understood. “You mean Sister Luo?” “Yes.” She got out of bed, her eyes still heavy with sleep but her face alight with excitement. “They can hold the wedding in Shanghai, with two wives of equal standing in separate households. Then she can have both the decorated bridal chair and the red skirt. What do you think?” “Everyone knows Little Uncle already has a principal wife in Hangzhou. What will they say when people ask?” “He can be heir to two family branches!” she answered at once. “Who's going to investigate their genealogy?” “There's something in that. I wonder whether Little Uncle would agree.” “That's for him to decide. We matchmakers will at least have offered a solution. Besides, I don't think he'll refuse.” Gu considered the idea and agreed to it, asking only, “What happens when she goes back to Hangzhou?” “Treat it like a bride's return visit to her parents: first she kowtows in the ancestral hall, then she meets the old lady and kowtows to her.” “That isn't a return visit to her parents. It's the formal presentation at the ancestral shrine. That would raise Sister Luo's standing.” Gu nodded emphatically. “It could work.” “If you think so, it's settled. Ask Mr Wu this afternoon and see what he says.” “If it can be arranged that way, what objection could he have? But you're wrong to say it's settled. It can only be settled when Little Uncle agrees.” “Then write quickly and ask him.” Gu thought there was no need for such haste. He also thought there was no need to argue with his beloved wife over it: she would not know whether he had written or not. “I'll write,” he said.

zh: 乌先生上午去看了罗四姐，下午由古应春陪着他，坐了马车去观光，一圈兜下来，乌先生自己提出要求，想到古家来吃晚饭，为的是谈罗四姐的亲事。“我跟她谈过了，她说她的意思，七姑奶奶都晓得。不过，既然我是媒人，她说有些话，要我跟七姑奶奶来商量。““是的。乌先生你说。”第一件，将来两家是不是当亲戚来往，现在暂且可以不管。不过，她的女儿，要胡太太认做子女儿，将来要到胡家来的，下人要叫她‘干小姐’。““胡太太的儿女，还要叫她妹妹。”七姑奶奶补充着，极有把握他说：“这件事包在我身上。”“第二件比较麻烦，她说七姑奶奶答应了她的，要我请问七姑奶奶，不晓得是啥办法？”“办法是想到一个，不过，还不敢作主。这个办法，一定要胡大先生点了头才能算数。”“是的，做媒本来要双方自己愿意，象七姑奶奶这样爽快有担当，肯代胡大先生作主，真是难得。”乌先生可说：“不过，先谈谈也不要紧。”
en: Mr Wu visited Luo that morning. In the afternoon, Gu took him sightseeing by carriage, and when they had completed their tour, Mr Wu himself asked to dine at the Gu house so that they could discuss the marriage. “I've talked to her. She says the Seventh Lady knows what she wants. Still, since I'm acting as matchmaker, she has asked me to discuss a few points with you.” “Yes, Mr Wu. Please go ahead.” “First, whether the two families will deal with each other as relatives by marriage can be left aside for now. But she wants Mrs Hu to take her daughter as a god-daughter. The girl will be visiting the Hu house, and the servants must address her as the family's young god-daughter.” “And Mrs Hu's children must call her their younger sister,” the Seventh Lady added with complete confidence. “Leave that to me.” “The second point is more difficult. She says you made her a promise, and she has asked me to find out what arrangement you have in mind.” “We have thought of one, but I can't commit us to it yet. Mr Hu must approve it before it can be agreed.” “Of course. In matchmaking, both parties must consent. It is rare to find someone so decisive and ready to take responsibility on Mr Hu's behalf as you are. But there can be no harm in discussing it first.”

zh: 这件事很有关系，七姑奶奶心想，倘或自己说错了一句话，要收回或更改就不漂亮了，不如让她丈夫去谈，自己在一旁察言观色，适时加以纠正或者补充，比较妥当。于是古应春便在她授意之下，讲他们夫妇这天清早商量好的办法。讲得一点不错，七姑奶奶认为无需作何修正。倒是乌先生的态度，让她奇怪，只见他一面听，一面锁紧眉头，她不知道这是乌先生在用心思索一件事时，惯有的样子，只当他对这样的办法还不满意，心里不免大起反感。于是等古应春讲完了，她冷冷地问：“乌先生觉得这个办法，还有啥欠缺的地方？”“不是欠缺，我看很不妥当。”这就连古应春都诧异了，“乌先生，请你说个道理看。”他问“何以不妥当。”“胡大先生现在是天下闻名的人，佩服他、赞成他的人很多，妒忌他、要他好看的人也不少。万一京里的御史老爷参上一本，不得了。”“参上一本？参胡大先生？”“这我就不懂。”七姑奶奶接着也说，“犯了啥错？御史要参他。”“七姑奶奶，请你耐耐心，听我说……”
en: The matter was consequential. If she herself said something wrong, the Seventh Lady thought, it would look awkward to withdraw or alter it. Better to let her husband explain while she watched Mr Wu's expression and supplied a correction or addition at the right moment. At her prompting, Gu described the plan they had discussed that morning. He explained it perfectly, and she felt no need to amend anything. Mr Wu's manner, however, puzzled her. As he listened, his brows drew together. She did not know this was simply his customary expression when thinking hard; she supposed that he was dissatisfied with their proposal and began to resent it. When Gu had finished, she asked coldly, “What does Mr Wu find lacking in this arrangement?” “It isn't a matter of something lacking. I think it is very inappropriate.” Now even Gu was astonished. “Please tell us why. What is inappropriate about it?” “Mr Hu is famous throughout the country. Many people admire and support him, but plenty are jealous and would like to teach him a lesson. If one of the censors in the capital submitted an impeachment, it could cause serious trouble.” “An impeachment? Against Mr Hu?” “I don't understand either,” the Seventh Lady put in. “What wrong would he have committed for a censor to impeach him?” “Seventh Lady, please be patient and let me explain.”

zh: 原来乌先生的先世是杭州府钱塘县的刑房书办，已历四代，现在由乌先生的长兄承袭，《大清律例》是他的家学，对“户婚律”当然亦很熟悉，所以能为古应春夫妇作一番很详细的解释。他说，以“兼祧”为取“两头大”的借口，是刁俗如此，而律无明文，不过既然习俗相沿，官府亦承认的，只是兼祧亦有一定的规矩，如俗语所说的“两房台一子”，方准兼桃，这在胡雪岩的情形，显然不合。“你们两位请想，即称‘胡大先生’及有‘胡二先生’，好比合肥李家，有‘李大先生’李瀚章，就一定有‘李二先生’李鸿章。胡大先生既然有兄弟，就可以承继给他无子的叔伯，何用他来兼祧？”“这话说得有道理，‘胡大先生’这个称呼，就摆明了他是有兄弟的。”古应春对他妻子说：“兼桃这两个字，无论如何用不上。”“用不上就不能娶两房正室。一定要这么办，且不说大清律上怎么样，论官常先就有亏了，这叫做‘宠妾灭妻’，御史老爷一本参上去，事实俱在，逃都逃不了的。”
en: Mr Wu's forebears had served as clerks in the criminal section of the Qiantang county office in Hangzhou Prefecture for four generations. His eldest brother had now inherited the post. The Great Qing Code was a family field of learning, and he was naturally familiar with its provisions on households and marriage. He could therefore give the couple a detailed explanation. Using succession to two family branches as a pretext for taking two wives of equal standing, he said, was a crafty practice established by custom, with no explicit basis in the code. Since the custom had long been followed, the authorities did recognize it, but only under certain conditions. As the saying went, there must be “one son between two branches” before he could serve as heir to both. Hu Xueyan's case plainly failed to meet that requirement. “Consider his title. If there is an Eldest Mr Hu, there is also a Second Mr Hu. It is like the Li family of Hefei: where there is an Eldest Mr Li, Li Hanzhang, there must be a Second Mr Li, Li Hongzhang. Since Mr Hu has brothers, one of them could be adopted as heir by a childless uncle. Why should he himself have to carry on two branches?” “That makes sense. Calling him Eldest Mr Hu shows plainly that he has brothers.” Turning to his wife, Gu said, “Whatever else we do, we cannot invoke succession to two branches.” “And without that, he cannot take two principal wives. If he insists, quite apart from what the Qing code may say, he will already have violated the standards expected of an official. This is called favouring a concubine at the expense of one's wife. A censor need only submit an impeachment: the facts would be there, with no way of evading them.”

zh: 一听这话，七姑奶奶吓出一身冷汗，“真是亏得乌先生指点，”她说，“差点做错了事情，害我们小爷叔栽个筋斗。”“筋斗倒也栽不大，不过面子难看。”乌先生又说：“讲老实话，胡大先生还在其次，我先要替罗四姐想一想，倘或因为她想坐花轿、穿红裙，弄出来这场麻烦，胡老太太、胡大先生一定很不高兴，说风凉知的人就会说：‘一进门就出事，一定是个扫帚星。’七姑奶奶你倒想，罗四姐以后还好做人？”“乌先生，你想得真周到，见识真正高人一等。”七姑奶奶由衷的佩服，“而且人家本来不知道罗四姐是啥身分，这一来‘妾’的名声就‘卖朝报’了。”“卖朝报”是句杭州的俗话，还是南宋时候传下来的，老百姓的名字忽然在“朝报”上出现，一定出了新闻，“卖朝报”的人为广招徕，必然大声吆喝，以至大街小巷，无人不知。如果胡雪岩因为“宠妾灭妻”而奉旨申斥，上谕中就会有罗四姐的名字。清朝的“宫门抄”就是南宋的“朝报”，所以七姑奶奶的这个譬喻，十分贴切。“是啊！”乌先生说，“那一来，不但杭州上海，到处都知道了，真正叫做‘求荣反辱’。我想我只要一说明白，罗四姐一定也懂的。”“是，是！”古应春忽忙接口，“那就拜托先生跟罗四姐婉言解释。只要讲一层讲通了，我想我们的这个媒就做成功了。”
en: The Seventh Lady broke into a cold sweat. “It's fortunate you explained this, Mr Wu. I nearly made a mistake that could have brought Little Uncle down.” “The fall would not be very serious, but it would look bad. To tell the truth, Mr Hu is my second concern. I must think of Sister Luo first. If her wish for a decorated bridal chair and a red skirt brought on all this trouble, Old Madam Hu and Mr Hu would certainly be displeased. Those inclined to sneer would say, ‘Trouble the moment she enters the house! She must bring bad luck.’ Think how hard her life would be after that.” “You have considered everything, Mr Wu. Your judgement is truly exceptional.” The Seventh Lady's admiration was sincere. “Besides, people might not originally have known her status. Then the fact that she was a concubine would be hawked about like the Court Gazette.” “Hawking the Court Gazette” was a Hangzhou expression handed down from the Southern Song. If an ordinary person's name suddenly appeared in the gazette, something newsworthy must have happened. The sellers would shout it out to attract customers until everyone in every street and alley knew. If Hu were reprimanded by imperial decree for favouring a concubine at his wife's expense, Luo's name would appear in the edict. The Qing Palace Gate Bulletin corresponded to the Southern Song Court Gazette, making the Seventh Lady's comparison especially apt. “Exactly,” Mr Wu said. “Then people everywhere would know, not just in Hangzhou and Shanghai. She would truly have sought honour and gained disgrace. I think she'll understand once I explain it clearly.” “Yes, yes!” Gu put in hastily. “Then please explain it to her tactfully. If we can settle this one point, I think our match will be made.”

zh: 罗四姐自然能够体谅其中的苦衷，但总觉得快快有不足之意，不过对七姑奶奶极力帮她讲话出主意，非常感激，因而也就更觉得可以说知心话，所以反而拿乌先生向她解释的话，来跟七姑奶奶商量。“四姐，我想劝你一句话，英雄不怕出身低，一个人要收缘结果好，才是真正的风光。你不是心胸不开阔的人，不要再在这上头计较了。”七姑奶又说：“我当你陪嫁的奶妈，送了你去，你看好不好？”江浙风俗，富家小姐出阁时，贴身的侍女、哺育的乳母，往往都陪嫁到夫家，而且保留着原来的称呼。罗四姐听七姑奶奶用这样的说法，表示就算委屈，她亦愿意分担，这份情意，求之于同胞姐妹，亦未见得必有，应该能够弥补一切了。“七姐，”罗四姐眼圈红红他说：“我也不知道前世敲破了多少木鱼，今生才会认识你。”“认识我没有啥了不得，倒是你嫁我们小爷叔，真是前世修来的。”七姑奶奶说：“做个女人家，无非走一步帮夫运，天大的本事，也是有限制的，丈夫是个阿斗太子，哪怕你是诸葛亮，也只好叹口气。我们小爷叔的本事，现在用出来的，不过十之二三，你能再把他那七、八分挖出来，你就是女人家当中第一等人物，何在乎名分上头？”
en: Naturally Luo could appreciate the difficulty, but she still felt disappointed and dissatisfied. At the same time, she was deeply grateful to the Seventh Lady for speaking up for her and trying so hard to find a solution. Feeling all the more able to confide in her, she brought Mr Wu's explanation back for discussion. “Let me offer you a little advice,” the Seventh Lady said. “A hero need not fear a humble beginning. It is a good outcome that brings real honour. You aren't a narrow-minded woman; don't keep dwelling on this. I'll be your dowry wet nurse and go with you to your new home. How would that be?” In Jiangsu and Zhejiang, when a girl from a wealthy family married, her personal maid and the wet nurse who had brought her up often accompanied her to her husband's home, retaining their old titles. In putting it this way, the Seventh Lady was saying that, if there was humiliation to endure, she was willing to share it. Such affection was not always to be found even between sisters of the same blood; it ought to make up for everything. “Seventh Sister,” Luo said, her eyes reddening, “I wonder how many wooden prayer fish I must have worn out in a previous life to earn the chance of knowing you in this one.” “Knowing me is nothing remarkable. Marrying Little Uncle is the blessing you earned in a former life. A woman can only help her husband prosper; however great her abilities, they have their limits. If her husband is an incapable Prince Adou, even a Zhuge Liang can do nothing but sigh. Little Uncle has so far used only two or three tenths of his ability. If you can bring out the remaining seven or eight tenths, you will rank among the finest of women. Why worry about formal status?”

zh: 听这一说，顿时激起罗四姐的万丈雄心，很兴奋他说：“七姐，我同你说心里的话，我自己也常在想，我如果是个男的，一样有把握创一番名堂出来，只可惜是个女的。如今胡大先生虽说把个家交给我，我看他倒也并非一定只限制我把家当好了就好了，在生意上头，如何做法，他也会听我的，我倒很想下手试一试。”“是的。”七姑奶奶很婉转他说：“不过，这到底在其次，你出了主意，是好的，他一定会听，那就等于你自己在做，并不一定要你亲自下手。照我看，你的顶大的一桩生意是开矿，开人矿。这话你懂不懂？”“不懂。七姐，”罗四姐笑道：“你的花样真多。”“我是实实在在的话，不是耍花佯。我刚刚说道，你要把我们小爷叔没有用出来的七、八分本事，把它挖出来。如果你做得到，你就是开着了一座金矿！别的都算小生意了。”罗四姐先当七姑奶奶是说笑话，听完了细细思量，方始逐渐领悟，庄容说道：“七姐，你的这番道理我懂了。不过，以前我没有想到这一点，只想到要逞自己的本事，现在才晓得，我要逞本事，一定要从胡大先生身上去下功夫。”“对啊！”七姑奶奶高兴地拍着手说：“你到底聪明，想得透，看得透。”
en: These words awakened boundless ambition in Luo. “Seventh Sister, I'll tell you what I really think,” she said excitedly. “I've often thought that, if I were a man, I could certainly make something of myself. It's just my misfortune to be a woman. Mr Hu says he is putting the household in my hands, but I don't think he necessarily means to limit me to keeping it in order. He will listen to my ideas about business too. I'd very much like to try my hand at it.” “Yes,” the Seventh Lady said tactfully, “though that comes second. If your ideas are good, he will certainly take your advice, and that amounts to doing the work yourself; you needn't carry it out with your own hands. In my view, your greatest enterprise will be mining—mining a man's abilities. Do you understand?” “No.” Luo laughed. “You have so many tricks, Seventh Sister.” “I'm quite serious. This isn't a trick. As I just said, you must dig out the seven or eight tenths of Little Uncle's ability that he hasn't yet used. If you can do that, you'll have opened a gold mine. Every other business will be a small affair beside it.” At first Luo had thought she was joking. Now she considered the words carefully and gradually understood. “I see what you mean,” she said gravely. “It hadn't occurred to me before. I thought only of showing what I could do myself. Now I understand that, to demonstrate my own ability, I must devote my efforts to bringing out Mr Hu's.” “Exactly!” The Seventh Lady clapped her hands with pleasure. “You are clever, after all. You can think things through and see to the heart of them.”

zh: 除了“迎亲”的花轿以外，其余尽量照“六礼”的规矩来办，先换庚帖，然后下聘，聘礼是两万现银，存在杭州阜康钱庄生息，供罗四姐为老娘养老之用，当然还有一座房子，仍旧置在螺狮门外。罗四姐在上海的新居，亦已过户在她名下，七姑奶奶所垫的房价及其他费用，自然是由胡雪岩结算。聘礼最重首饰，只得四样，不过较之寻常人家的八样，还更贵重，新穿的珠花、金刚钻的镯子、翡翠耳环、红玉簪子，其实是罗四姐自己挑的。胡雪岩关照古应春，请七姑奶奶陪罗四姐去选定了，叫珠宝店直接送到上海阜康钱庄，验货收款。
en: Only the decorated bridal chair for bringing her to her new home was omitted; in all other respects, the arrangements followed the Six Rites of marriage as closely as possible. First they exchanged cards bearing the birth dates and hours; then came the betrothal gifts. The monetary gift was twenty thousand taels of ready silver, deposited with Fukang Bank in Hangzhou to earn interest for Luo to support her mother. There was a house as well, again bought outside Luosimen. Luo's new home in Shanghai had also been transferred into her name, and Hu naturally settled the purchase price and other expenses advanced by the Seventh Lady. Jewellery was the most important part of the betrothal gifts. There were only four kinds, but they were more valuable than the eight kinds commonly given: newly strung pearl flowers, diamond bracelets, jade earrings, and red jade hairpins. Luo had chosen them herself. Hu had told Gu to ask the Seventh Lady to accompany her in making her selection, then have the jeweller deliver the pieces directly to the Shanghai branch of Fukang Bank for inspection and payment.

zh: “四姐，应春昨天跟我说：你们情同姐妹，这一回等于我们嫁妹子，应该要备一份嫁妆。这话一点不错。”七姑奶奶说：“我想，仍旧你自己去挑，大家的面子，你尽管拣好的挑，不要客气。说老实话，几千两银子，应春的力量还有。”罗四姐心想，只要嫁到胡家，将来一定有许多机会帮古应春的忙，借为补报，所以不必说客气话。不过，也不好意思让他们多破费，因而这样答说：“七姐跟姐夫这番意思，我不能不领。不过，东西也不在乎贵重，只要欢喜就好，你说是不是？”“正是。”七姑奶奶说：“先挑木器。明天你空不空。”“空。”“那就明天下半天。仍旧到昌发去好了。”昌发在南市，是上海最大的一家木器行，罗四姐新居的家具，就是在那里买的，“好！就是昌发。”罗四姐说，“今天家里会有客人来，我要走了。”等七姑奶奶用马车将她送到家，罗四姐立即关照老马，另雇一辆马车，要带小大姐到南市去办事。
en: “Yingchun said to me yesterday that, since we're as close as sisters, this is like marrying off a sister of our own, and we ought to provide a dowry. He's quite right,” the Seventh Lady told Luo. “I think you should choose that yourself too. For all our sakes, pick the best and don't stand on ceremony. To be frank, Yingchun can still afford a few thousand taels.” Once she was married into the Hu family, Luo thought, there would be plenty of opportunities to help Gu and repay his kindness. There was no need for polite refusals. Still, she was embarrassed to let them spend too much. “I can't refuse such kindness from you and Brother-in-Law Gu. But things needn't be expensive. What matters is that one likes them, wouldn't you say?” “Exactly. Let's choose the furniture first. Are you free tomorrow?” “Yes.” “Then tomorrow afternoon. We may as well go to Changfa again.” Changfa Furniture Shop, in Nanshi, was the largest furniture firm in Shanghai. Luo had bought the furnishings for her new home there. “Good. Changfa it is. I'm expecting a visitor at home today, so I must go.” The Seventh Lady sent her home in her carriage. As soon as she arrived, Luo told Old Ma to hire another carriage: she wanted to take her maid to Nanshi on an errand.

zh: 到得南市在昌发下车，老板姓李，一见老主顾上门，忽忙亲自迎了出来招呼：“罗四小姐，今天怎么有空？请里面坐，里面坐。”“我来看堂木器。”“喔，喔！”李老板满脸堆笑，“是哪里用的？”“房间里。”所谓“房间里”是指卧房，首要的就是一张床，但既称“一堂”，当然应该还有几椅桌凳之类，李老板便先间材料，“罗四小姐喜欢红木，还是紫檀？”“当然是紫檀。”“罗四小姐，你既然喜欢紫檀，我有一堂难得的木器，不可错过机会。”“好！我来看看。”
en: When she alighted at Changfa in Nanshi, the owner, Mr Li, recognized his regular customer and hurried out to greet her himself. “Miss Luo, what brings you here today? Do come inside. Please, come in.” “I've come to look at a set of furniture.” “Ah, yes!” Mr Li was all smiles. “What room is it for?” “The bedroom.” A bedroom set meant, first and foremost, a bed, but since she wanted a whole set, it should naturally include tables, chairs, and stools as well. Mr Li began by asking about the material. “Would you prefer hongmu rosewood or zitan, Miss Luo?” “Zitan, of course.” “If you like zitan, I have a remarkable set. You mustn't miss the opportunity.” “Very well. Let me see it.”

zh: 李老板将她领入后进一个房间，进门便觉目眩，原来这些紫檀木器，以螺甸嵌花，有耀眼的反光，以致眩目。细细看去，华丽精巧，实在可爱，“这好象不是本地货色。”罗四姐说：“花样做法部不同。”“罗四小姐，到底是顶瓜瓜的行家，”李老板说：“一眼就只透了。这堂木器是广东来的，广东叫酸枝，就是紫檀。光是广东来的不稀奇，另外还有来历，说出来，罗四小姐，你要吓一跳。”“为啥？”“这本来是进贡的……”“进贡的？”罗四姐打断他的话说：“你是说，原来是皇帝用的。”“不错。”“李老板，”罗四姐笑道：“你说大话不怕豁边？皇帝用的木器，怎么会在你店里？”“喏，罗四小姐，你不相信是不是？其中当然有个道理。你请坐下来，等我讲给你听。”
en: Mr Li led her into a room at the back. The moment she entered, she was dazzled: the zitan furniture was decorated with mother-of-pearl inlay, which caught the light in brilliant flashes. On closer inspection, the pieces were splendid, delicately worked, and very appealing. “This doesn't look like local work,” Luo said. “The designs and workmanship are different.” “You really are a first-rate judge, Miss Luo. You saw it at a glance. This set came from Guangdong. They call the wood suanzhi there; it's what we call zitan. But coming from Guangdong is nothing extraordinary. It has a history that will astonish you.” “Why?” “It was originally made as tribute—” “Tribute?” she interrupted. “You mean it was originally for the emperor?” “Exactly.” “Mr Li,” she said with a laugh, “aren't you afraid a boast like that will burst at the seams? How could furniture meant for the emperor end up in your shop?” “You don't believe me, do you? There is naturally an explanation. Please sit down and let me tell you.”

zh: 李老板请罗四姐在一张交椅上坐了下来，自己在下首相陪。他很会做生意，用的伙计、徒弟亦很灵活，等罗四姐刚刚坐定，现泡的盖碗茶与四个高脚果碟，已经送了上来。罗四姐存心要来买木器，生意一定做得成，所以对昌发的款待，但然接受，连道声谢都没有。“罗四小姐，请你先仔细看看东西。”她原有此意。因为所坐的那张交椅，小巧玲珑，高低正好，靠背适度，一坐下来双时自然而然地搭在扶手上，非常舒服，本就想仔细看一看，所以听得这话，便低头细细赏鉴，工料两精，毫无瑕疵。看完交椅，再看椅旁的长方套几，一共三层，推拢了不占地位，拉开了颇为实用，一碗茶，四只果碟摆在上面，一点都不湿得挤。“东西是好的。”罗四姐说：“不过花样不象宫里用的，宫里用的应该是龙凤，不应该是‘五福捧寿，。”
en: Mr Li invited her to sit in an armchair and took a lower place beside her. He was an able businessman, and his clerks and apprentices were quick to act. She had scarcely sat down before freshly brewed tea in a covered bowl and four stemmed fruit dishes were brought in. Luo had come intending to buy furniture, and a sale was certain, so she accepted Changfa's hospitality without ceremony or even a word of thanks. “First, please take a good look at the pieces, Miss Luo.” She had intended to do just that. The armchair was compact and elegant, at exactly the right height, with a well-proportioned back. As soon as she sat down, her elbows rested naturally on the arms; it was extremely comfortable. Now she bent her head to examine it closely. Both the material and the craftsmanship were excellent, without a flaw. After the chair, she studied the rectangular nesting tables beside it. There were three, taking up little space when pushed together and proving very useful when drawn out. The tea bowl and all four fruit dishes stood on them without the least crowding. “The pieces are good,” Luo said. “But the design doesn't look like palace furniture. Surely palace pieces should have dragons and phoenixes, not ‘Five Blessings Supporting Longevity.’”
